name: KUWAIT

flag.title: State of Kuwait
flag.note: Green, white & red stripes; black trapezoid

lead: Kuwait is a small Gulf state. Oil turned its desert into one of Earth's wealthiest nations. Kuwaitis pay no income tax. Before oil, men dived for pearls and dhow traders sailed to India and Africa.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Kuwait is flat desert. Its highest point is just 306 metres, an unnamed hill in the west. Kuwait Bay gives the capital a natural harbour.
Kuwait has no rivers, no lakes and almost no rain. Drinking water comes from machines that turn seawater drinkable. Kuwait built its first desalination plant in 1951.
animals: The dromedary camel is Kuwait's national animal. It has one hump and can go a week without water. Camel races are huge events. Tiny robots steered by remote control ride as jockeys.
Every winter, thousands of flamingos wade the mudflats of Sulaibikhat Bay and turn the shore pink. Gentle dugongs, or sea cows, graze seagrass offshore. They are rare and fully protected.
culture: Kuwaitis are famous for hospitality. Every home has a diwaniya, a sitting room where guests drink cardamom coffee and share dates. It is rude to refuse the first tiny cup.
The national dish is machboos, spiced rice with slow-cooked lamb or fish. Before oil, men dived 12 m on one breath for pearls. A yearly festival still celebrates it.
history: Bani Khalid settlers built a small fort on Kuwait Bay in the 1670s. The name means 'little fort near water' in Arabic. The Al-Sabah family took charge around 1752.
Oil was found in 1938 and exports began in 1946. Iraq invaded in 1990 and burned over 600 oil wells. A US-led coalition freed Kuwait in 1991.
wows: One dinar is worth over three US dollars, the highest-value currency unit.
Burning oil wells took nine months to put out in 1991.
Kuwait has no natural freshwater at all.
Summer can top 50 °C, among the hottest places on Earth.
Robot jockeys have raced camels since 2005 to protect children.
The Kuwait Towers store fresh water in their globes.
Al-Hashemi-II is the world's largest wooden dhow, says Guinness.

myths.fact: Dry air holds little heat. Desert nights can turn cold soon after sunset.
Most oil comes from tiny sea plants and animals that died millions of years ago.
